newsitem.title: USA: Basin Electric 550 MW unit shut after up briefly.
newsitem.headline: Basin Electric 550 MW unit shut after up briefly.

text.p: Basin Electric Power Cooperative's 550 megawatt Laramie River Station (LRS) coal-fired unit 3 was shut again after resuming service briefly Wednesday, the utility said.
"It came up, and right back down," said said spokesman Stan Stelter.
The unit was taken out of service after deciding more boiler tube repairs were needed, he said. LRS 3 was originally shut last Saturday for the same problem.
"It could be one or two days," he replied when asked about a schedule when the unit 3 would return to operation.
The two neighboring units, each also at 550 MW, at the LRS facility were running at full output, Stelter said.
The three LRS units are located in Wheatland, Wyo.
Basin Electric, headquartered in Bismarck. N.D., is the operator of LRS and majority owner with a 42.27 percent stake. Five other Midwest public utilities co-own the plant.
